cultural_notes.title: Greeting Customs
cultural_notes.content: In Oromo culture, greetings are very important and can be quite elaborate. It's common to ask about family, health, and work when greeting someone.

cultural_notes.title: Respect for Elders
cultural_notes.content: Elders are highly respected in Oromo culture. When greeting an elder, it's polite to use formal language and show respect through body language.

cultural_notes.title: Coffee Ceremony
cultural_notes.content: Coffee (buna) plays a central role in Oromo social life. The coffee ceremony can last several hours and involves roasting, grinding, and brewing coffee in a special pot called a jebena.

cultural_notes.title: Gadaa System
cultural_notes.content: The Gadaa system is the traditional social organization of the Oromo people. It's a democratic system based on age grades with leaders elected every eight years.

cultural_notes.title: Irreecha Festival
cultural_notes.content: Irreecha is the Oromo Thanksgiving festival celebrated annually to thank Waaq (God) for the blessings of the previous year.
